title: Content Pack (v1)
description: A self-contained tabletop RPG content pack: one scenario (or a campaign frame, or a set of characters) plus everything a game master needs to run it at the table — briefing, acts with read-aloud narration and GM notes, a scene-by-scene runner, NPCs, threats, handouts, maps, endings and pre-generated characters. Packs are pure data rendered by a universe-agnostic engine; never put rules text, HTML or markdown tables in prose fields. Write in the voice and setting of the universe named in `universe`.

packVersion.description: Schema version of this pack. Always the integer 1 for this schema.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique within the universe (e.g. "derelict-signal-7c"). Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens only; 3–64 characters. Used as the file name on disk.

universe.description: Registry id of the universe this pack belongs to (e.g. "alien", "dune"). Determines theme, rules, attribute/skill keys and terminology.

kind.description: "scenario" = one playable adventure (requires at least one act). "campaign" = a campaign frame or multi-session arc (requires at least one act). "characters" = a roster of characters only, no acts needed. "maps" = a map overlay pack with id "<packId>-maps": its maps[] are merged by map id into pack <packId> at load (used by the Room Editor for bundled packs).

meta.description: Catalogue information shown in the scenario library and used for filtering.

title.description: Evocative title, 2–6 words, title case (e.g. "Chariot of the Gods"). No subtitle, no quotes.

tagline.description: One punchy sentence (8–25 words) that sells the premise and hints at the horror or stakes, like a film poster line. No spoilers of twists.

synopsis.description: GM-facing overview of the whole scenario in 2–5 sentences (60–150 words): the situation, what is really going on, the main threat and the shape of the climax. Spoilers allowed — players never see this.

type.description: Play style. "Cinematic" = one-shot with pre-generated characters, personal agendas and expected character death; "Campaign" = part of an ongoing campaign with persistent characters; "One-Shot" = standalone session without the cinematic agenda structure.

players.description: Recommended player count as a range or number, e.g. "3–5" or "4".

playtime.description: Expected real-world play time, e.g. "3–4 hours" or "2 sessions".

difficulty.description: Short difficulty label for the GM, e.g. "Introductory", "Standard", "Hard", "Extreme", or "Advanced Cinematic".

tone.description: 2–5 lowercase tone keywords that describe how the scenario should feel, e.g. ["dread", "isolation", "corporate betrayal"].

items.description: A single lowercase tone keyword or short phrase.

contentWarnings.description: Lowercase content warnings the GM should discuss with players before play, e.g. ["body horror", "child endangerment"]. Empty array if none.

generated.description: Provenance for machine-generated packs. Omit for hand-written packs.

params.description: The generation parameters exactly as submitted (players, playtime, tone, setting hints, etc.). Open map; any keys allowed.

source.description: Where the pack came from: "bundled" = shipped inside the app, "custom" = written or imported by a user, "generated" = produced by the AI generator.

briefing.description: The in-world opening transmission shown to players before Act I — a memo, order or computer message in the universe's voice (for ALIEN: terse MU/TH/UR or corporate/military teletype).

from.description: Sender line in upper case, e.g. "MU/TH/UR 6000 MAINFRAME" or "USCM COMMAND — FORT NEBRASKA".

to.description: Recipient line in upper case, e.g. "CREW, USCSS MONTERO".

classification.description: Classification or priority line in upper case, e.g. "PRIORITY ONE — COMPANY DIRECTIVE".

text.description: The briefing body: 120–350 words in 3–7 short paragraphs separated by blank lines, written entirely in-world (no rules, no GM asides). It should state the mission, hint at what is being withheld, and end with a sign-off.

acts.description: The scenario's acts in play order. Cinematic scenarios use exactly three (e.g. HOPE → DOUBT → HORROR). Required (at least one) for kind "scenario" and "campaign".

npcs.description: Important non-player characters the GM portrays, 3–8 for a typical scenario.

threats.description: Creatures and hostile forces the players may face, from first glimpse to final form.

keyLocations.description: Places the action moves through, 4–10 entries, each a sensory, gameable description.

name.description: Location name, optionally prefixed with the vessel or site, e.g. "USCSS Cronus — Lab Module".

description.description: 1–3 sentences (20–60 words): what it looks, sounds and smells like, and what can happen or be found there.

handouts.description: In-world messages the GM can push to players' phones as transmissions during play: orders, intercepted logs, private agenda updates. 2–6 per scenario.

clues.description: Secrets and clues the GM can reveal to one, several or all players with one tap (Three Clue Rule: give every important conclusion at least three clues). Scenes point at them with clueRefs. 0–12 per scenario.

clocks.description: Progress clocks the GM ticks during play: a danger approaching, a race against time, or a tug-of-war. Visible clocks render on the table board and the players' phones. 0–6 per scenario.

maps.description: Maps for the GM screen: ASCII schematics drawn with box-drawing characters, or images by URL.

endings.description: Possible outcomes the GM narrates at the end, 2–4 entries covering success, pyrrhic victory and total loss.

title.description: Short ending name in upper case, e.g. "ESCAPE IN THE EEV".

condition.description: What must be true for this ending, in one sentence of GM language.

text.description: Read-aloud epilogue, 1–3 paragraphs of second-person or cinematic narration (60–200 words), no rules text.

characters.description: Pre-generated player characters embedded in the pack (Cinematic scenarios: one per expected player, typically 4–5, each with a personal agenda that conflicts with at least one other character's).

tips.description: Practical advice for the GM running this pack, 3–8 one-sentence tips (pacing, when to spring events, how to handle player-vs-player conflict).

items.description: One concrete, actionable sentence of GM advice.

title.description: Act label in upper case, e.g. "ACT I".

subtitle.description: One or two upper-case words naming the act's mood or theme, e.g. "HOPE", "THE LONG NIGHT".

summary.description: GM-facing one or two sentence summary of what happens in this act.

readAloud.description: 2–6 paragraphs of second-person present-tense narration the GM (or text-to-speech) reads to players, each 40–120 words. Pure atmosphere and situation — no rules text, no dice, no GM secrets, no stage directions.

items.description: One narration paragraph, 40–120 words, second person, present tense.

gmNotes.description: Private GM guidance for the act in 1–3 paragraphs: what is really happening, which events to trigger, how agendas should start to bite, and how to pace toward the next act.

agendaNotes.description: How the characters' personal agendas should develop during this act (subtle in Act I, conflicting in Act II, open betrayal in Act III).

sceneArt.description: Optional image (site path such as "/art/scenes/pad-b.webp" or an https URL) shown full-bleed on the table board in theatre-of-mind mode while this act runs.

scenes.description: Ordered scene-by-scene runner the GM checks off during play, typically 3–8 per act.

scene.description: One scene or event in the scene runner.

name.description: Short evocative scene name, 1–5 words, e.g. "Mother Awakens".

mandatory.description: true if the plot needs this scene to happen; false if optional color or a contingency.

encounter.description: true if this scene contains a fight or a direct threat encounter.

encounterDetail.description: When encounter is true: what attacks, how many, key stats or behavior, and how it escalates or escapes. One to three sentences.

narration.description: What the GM describes or reads when the scene starts: 1–4 sentences, sensory and specific.

checks.description: Skill checks the scene calls for, each as "SKILL — purpose" or "SKILL at −2 — purpose" using the universe's skill names in upper case.

items.description: One skill check, e.g. "OBSERVATION — notice the elongated forearms".

events.description: Things that happen during the scene regardless of player action, in order.

stressTriggers.description: Stress or panic consequences, e.g. "STRESS +1 — all PCs present" or "IMMEDIATE PANIC ROLL — witnesses".

items.description: One stress or panic trigger with who it affects.

npcGuidance.description: How NPCs present in this scene behave, what they want and what they lie about.

gmTip.description: One or two sentences of practical advice for running the scene (pacing, reveals, what to hold back).

outcomes.description: Likely results of the scene and where each leads.

clueRefs.description: Ids of entries in the pack's clues[] that can be found in this scene.

ambient.description: Optional ambient audio cue for the scene: a universe audio preset id or a site path to an audio file.

name.description: Name as players would hear it, e.g. "Dr. Flynn" or "Ava 6".

role.description: Position or function in a few words, e.g. "Weyland-Yutani Representative".

agenda.description: What the NPC wants, in one sentence.

behavior.description: How to play them: demeanor, tells, what they do under pressure. One or two sentences.

secret.description: What the NPC hides from the players, if anything.

stats.description: Optional game statistics in the universe's own keys (e.g. {"health": 4, "rangedCombat": 3}). Open map.

name.description: Threat name, e.g. "Neomorph" or "UPP Spetsnaz squad".

ref.description: Id of a matching entry in the universe bestiary (e.g. "drone", "neomorph") so the GM can open full stats.

description.description: What it looks like and how it is first encountered, in 1–2 sentences.

stats.description: Optional statistics in the universe's own keys (e.g. {"speed": 2, "health": 7, "armor": 8}). Open map.

tactics.description: How the threat behaves and escalates over the scenario, in 1–3 sentences.

handout.description: An in-world message the GM can send to players as a transmission.

id.description: kebab-case id unique within the pack.

title.description: Short handout title in upper case, e.g. "SPECIAL ORDER 966".

to.description: Intended recipient: a character name, a role, or "ALL CREW".

priority.description: Priority label shown on the player's phone; prefer one of the universe's priorities (ALIEN: STANDARD, PRIORITY, EYES ONLY, EMERGENCY).

text.description: The message body, 20–200 words, fully in-world in teletype style. No GM notes.

when.description: When the GM should send it, e.g. "Act II, after the logs are recovered".

image.description: Optional image shown with the handout on the phone (and full-bleed on the board when the GM pushes it there): a site path such as "/art/handouts/manifest.webp" or an https URL.

clue.description: A secret or clue the players can discover.

id.description: kebab-case id unique within the pack.

text.description: What the players learn, as the GM would tell or show it, in one or two sentences (no rules text).

source.description: Where or from whom it can be found, e.g. "Abram's maintenance log".

scene.description: Name of the scene where it is most likely found (optional; scenes may also list it in clueRefs).

status.description: Initial status: "hidden" (default) or "revealed" for something the players know from the start.

id.description: kebab-case id unique within the pack.

label.description: Short upper-case label shown on the board, e.g. "REACTOR MELTDOWN" or "RESCUE SHIP ARRIVES".

segments.description: Number of segments: 4 (soon), 6 (a while), 8 (long haul) or another count from 2 to 12.

filled.description: Segments already filled at the start (default 0).

kind.description: "danger" = strikes when full; "racing" = the players' progress racing a danger; "tug" = a tug-of-war that can move both ways.

visibility.description: "all" = shown on the board and phones; "gm" = the GM's eyes only.

note.description: What happens when the clock fills, for the GM.

map.description: A map for the GM screen.

id.description: kebab-case id unique within the universe's maps, e.g. "uscss-cronus".

title.description: Map title in upper case, e.g. "USCSS CRONUS".

subtitle.description: Class, designation or region line, e.g. "Weyland-Yutani Science Vessel — Derelict".

description.description: One or two sentences of GM context for the location.

kind.description: "ascii" = schematic drawn in the `ascii` field; "image" = picture at `src`; "engine" = interactive deck plan registered by the universe (`engine`).

ascii.description: Required when kind is "ascii": a monospace schematic drawn with box-drawing characters (╔═╗║┌─┐│└┘), at most ~70 columns wide, with labelled rooms and a title block.

src.description: Required when kind is "image": absolute URL path of the image, e.g. "/maps/acm/talos-station.png".

engine.description: Optional id of an interactive MapEngine deck plan registered by the universe (e.g. "uscss-montero"); the GM screen offers it alongside this map.

size.description: Optional source size [width, height] in px (image maps: the image natural size). Rooms stay normalized.

levels.description: Optional decks/levels; rooms and tokens carry a level id.

rooms.description: Labelled areas on the map with short GM notes.

id.description: kebab-case room id unique within the map (needed for the table board fog).

name.description: Room or area name as labelled on the map.

level.description: Level id this room is on (multi-level maps).

shape.description: Room outline in normalized map space (0..1 of the map width/height). rect: x, y, w, h. poly: points [[x,y],...] (3+).

spawn.description: Default drop points (normalized) for new tokens.

grid.description: Optional grid cell size as a fraction of the map width (token size 1 = one cell). Default 1/40.

outline.description: Optional hull/outline SVG path in normalized coordinates; the table board dims everything outside it.

crop.description: Optional normalized region the table board fits to the screen.

levelNoun.description: Optional word the table board uses for levels of this map, e.g. "DECK", "FLOOR", "LEVEL".

backdrop.description: Optional table-board backdrop behind the map: "space" (star field), "sand" (dunes) or "none".

palette.description: Optional table-board palette overrides for this map (keys of the universe theme.board palette, e.g. fog, fogEdge, label, door, deck). Open map.

character.description: A player character, shaped by the universe's rules. Attribute and skill keys must be the universe's keys (ALIEN: attributes str/agi/wit/emp 2–5; skills heavyMachinery, stamina, closeCombat, mobility, piloting, rangedCombat, observation, comtech, survival, manipulation, medicalAid, command 0–5).

id.description: kebab-case id unique across the universe, e.g. "cpt-miller".

name.description: Full name with rank or title if any, e.g. "Captain Lucas Miller".

career.description: Career name, ideally one of the universe's careers (ALIEN: Colonial Marine, Colonial Marshal, Company Agent, Kid, Medic, Officer, Pilot, Roughneck, Scientist).

appearance.description: 2–3 sentences of physical description and manner a player can perform.

attributes.description: Attribute scores keyed by the universe's attribute keys. Open map.

skills.description: Skill levels keyed by the universe's skill keys; include every skill, using 0 for untrained. Open map.

health.description: Optional starting health. The engine recomputes it from the universe rules on assignment, so this is informational only.

talent.description: One talent in the form "Name — effect in one sentence".

gear.description: 3–6 carried items, including the signature item.

signatureItem.description: A personal keepsake with a one-sentence story, e.g. "Dented coffee thermos — been with him through every voyage."

personalAgenda.description: The character's secret or personal goal for the scenario, 1–3 sentences in second person. In Cinematic play it must conflict with at least one other character's agenda.

agendaByAct.description: Optional replacement agendas handed out at the start of each act, keyed by act number as a string ("1", "2", "3"). Later acts should escalate toward betrayal.

^[1-9][0-9]?$.description: The agenda for that act, 1–3 sentences in second person.

buddy.description: Name of the character this PC trusts most (another PC or 'None').

rival.description: Name of the character this PC distrusts most (another PC or 'None').

secret.description: Optional hidden truth known only to this character's player (e.g. they are a synthetic).

driveStatements.description: One-line belief statement per attribute, keyed by the universe's attribute keys, for universes whose attributes carry a prompt (DUNE drives: duty, faith, justice, power, truth). Shown under each attribute on the character sheet; players can rewrite them in the character builder. Keep them out of appearance. Bundled and generated DUNE characters carry all five.

additionalProperties.description: One sentence in the character's voice.
